task.summary: Product-focused MakeLark homepage with an interactive Studio example

assumptions: The homepage explains an in-development product and uses fictional business examples.
An email-draft contact route is acceptable until a real submission endpoint exists.

techniques.rationale: Reproducible Xenia sampling generated a 48-candidate pool before selection.
Compared three materially different rendered hero compositions.
Applied the bundled pinned expander once; increased product proof without increasing homepage scope.
Separate reviewer inspected the implementation and interactions; preserves its actual score of 8.2. Strict context isolation is not established.
Reused existing supplied generated business images in fictional examples and the original identity assets.
Selected brief user-triggered feedback with reduced-motion behavior. No timed choreography or generated video.
Reviewed structural focus, required disclosures and mobile density.
Scanned and adjudicated craft signals in context; no authorship claim.
Reviewed every lint signal and preserved verified mobile copy fixes.

gate.reason: Actual critic score 8.2 remains below target 9.0. Functional checks pass; the gate is honest review evidence, not a claim that the homepage is unusable.

knowledge.fact: MakeLark Studio is the website product; MakeLark is the parent identity.
Studio is in development; all demonstration behavior is local and illustrative.
Homepage only and no ChatGPT Sites.

research.source: Xenia current repository guidance and supplied brand guide
research.limitation: No customer interviews or competitor usability study claimed.

metaphors.mapping: Owner request becomes a clearly visible website edit
metaphors.boundary: No AI model or live publishing is executed

metaphors.mapping: Studio workbench with tools and drafts
metaphors.boundary: Physical workbench decoration adds no product understanding

metaphors.mapping: Business change and website change stay in step
metaphors.boundary: Use shared timing/cause-and-effect only, not abstract motion

metaphors.mapping: Architectural precision and approachable brand warmth
metaphors.boundary: Business photographs stay in examples; no claims that photos depict real customers

decisions.reason: Clear product mechanism and tangible business result.

candidates.name: The working Studio
candidates.premise: Understand the product by trying one useful local change
candidates.composition: Outcome-led typography above a dominant website canvas and review rail
candidates.strength: Immediate product recognition and a concrete differentiator
candidates.risk: Demo must remain legible; avoid overly dense dashboard chrome

candidates.name: The business gallery
candidates.premise: Recognize the value through finished business website examples
candidates.composition: Centered promise followed by three differently sized photographic business-site panels
candidates.strength: Tangible business range and attractive output
candidates.risk: May read as an agency portfolio or template marketplace; evidence-heavy

candidates.name: The day after launch
candidates.premise: Website improves as the business changes
candidates.composition: Asymmetric headline with change history rail beside one evolving site
candidates.risk: Weak initial product/category recognition; better as a supporting section
